name: Disable NTFS Last-Access Timestamps
description: Stops NTFS writing a timestamp every time a file is merely read. Removes a write for every read on busy volumes, which matters most on directories with very many small files.

name: Enable NTFS Last-Access Timestamps
description: Restores last-access timestamp tracking, which some backup and forensic tools rely on to tell what has been read.

name: Disable 8.3 Short Name Creation
description: Stops NTFS generating a legacy PROGRA~1-style name alongside every long filename. Speeds up creating files in large directories. Very old 16-bit installers may object.

name: Enable Paths Longer Than 260 Characters
description: Lifts the MAX_PATH limit for applications that opt in, which is what stops deeply nested node_modules and build trees failing to copy or delete.

name: Increase NTFS Paged Pool Memory
description: Lets NTFS cache more metadata in paged pool, which helps on volumes with millions of files. Costs a modest amount of kernel memory.

name: Disable NTFS Compression
description: Blocks new NTFS-compressed files and folders. Compression trades CPU for space and can hurt on fast SSDs; existing compressed files are left alone.

name: Disable the Encrypting File System (EFS)
description: Turns off per-file EFS encryption. Worth doing if you use BitLocker instead, since EFS-encrypted files become unreadable if the user certificate is ever lost.

name: Enable TRIM for SSDs
description: Makes Windows tell an SSD which blocks are no longer in use, which is what keeps write performance from degrading over time.

name: Disable Storage Sense
description: Stops Windows automatically deleting temporary files, emptying the Recycle Bin and clearing the Downloads folder on a schedule.

name: Enable Storage Sense
description: Lets Windows reclaim disk space on its own by clearing temporary files and old Recycle Bin contents. It will not touch your Downloads folder unless separately configured.

name: Disable Reserved Storage
description: Frees the roughly 7 GB Windows sets aside for updates and temporary files. Feature updates may then need you to free space by hand before they will install.

name: Delete Files Immediately Instead of Recycling
description: Bypasses the Recycle Bin entirely, so deleted files are gone at once. There is no undo after this — consider carefully.

name: Send Deleted Files to the Recycle Bin
description: Restores normal deletion behaviour, so files go to the Recycle Bin and can be recovered.

name: Disable Scheduled Drive Optimisation
description: Turns off the weekly ScheduledDefrag task. On an SSD this task issues TRIM rather than defragmenting, so leaving it on is usually the better choice.

name: Disable the Disk Diagnostic Data Collector
description: Disables the scheduled task that gathers SMART and disk health data for reporting to Microsoft. Windows still warns you about a failing disk through other means.

name: Disable System Restore Shadow Copies
description: Stops Windows keeping restore points and previous file versions, which frees the shadow-copy space on the system drive. This also removes your ability to roll back a bad driver or update — including via this app's own restore points.

name: Enable System Restore
description: Allows Windows to keep restore points again, which is what lets you roll back a bad driver or update.

name: Optimise Removable Drives for Quick Removal
description: Turns off write caching on removable drives so a USB stick can be unplugged without ejecting it first. Slower writes, far fewer corrupted sticks.

name: Make USB Storage Read-Only
description: Blocks writes to removable storage devices while still allowing them to be read. A blunt but effective control against data walking out on a USB stick.

name: Allow Writing to USB Storage
description: Removes the removable-storage write block so USB drives can be written to normally.

name: Disable Windows Backup Reminders
description: Stops the recurring 'back up your files to OneDrive' prompts in Settings and File Explorer.

name: Stop OneDrive Starting With Windows
description: Removes OneDrive from the per-user startup list. Files already synced stay on disk; nothing is deleted.

name: Block OneDrive Personal Account Sync
description: Stops OneDrive syncing with personal Microsoft accounts while leaving work and school accounts able to connect.

name: Stop Keeping Application Crash Dumps
description: Turns off the local crash-dump archive Windows Error Reporting keeps under your profile, which quietly accumulates hundreds of megabytes.

name: Write Small Memory Dumps on a Blue Screen
description: Switches crash dumps from the automatic (potentially many-gigabyte) kernel dump to a 256 KB minidump. Still enough for most blue-screen analysis.

name: Disable the Low Disk Space Warning
description: Suppresses the balloon that appears when a drive drops below ten percent free, useful on a small system drive you deliberately keep near full.

name: Disable File History
description: Turns off the File History backup engine, which continuously copies your libraries to a second drive.

name: Pause Search Indexing on Battery
description: Stops the search indexer running while the laptop is unplugged, which is one of the larger avoidable battery drains on a machine with a big mail store.

name: Do Not Index Encrypted Files
description: Keeps EFS-encrypted file contents out of the search index, where they would otherwise sit in plaintext.
